Senses.PreferredTarget: The Accord of Difference and Sameness
AlternateTargets: Shitou's Accord of Difference and Sameness
Senses.Explanation: The title combines joining or taking part (參), sameness (同), and accord or tally (契): The Accord of Difference and Sameness. In the Chan corpus it names Shitou Xiqian's poem. Lamp records say Shitou wrote one piece called by this title, describe its wording as deep, and report that explanations circulated widely. The transmitted text begins, 'The heart of the great Indian immortal is intimately entrusted east and west' (竺土大仙心，東西密相付), then sets bright source against dark-flowing branches, asks how each field both interrelates and remains in its place, and closes, 'On hearing words you must meet the source; do not establish rules of your own ... I respectfully tell investigators of the mystery: do not waste the daylight' (承言須會宗，勿自立規矩……謹白參玄人，光陰莫虛度). A later lamp record links its composition to Shitou's reading, 'the sage has no self; there is nothing that is not himself' (聖人無己，靡所不己). The Zen deviation is bibliographic and lineage-specific: in these records the title is the proper name of Shitou's Chan verse, printed in full and repeatedly quoted inside later cases and comments.
Senses.Note: The corpus has 88 exact occurrences in 50 allowlisted files. It repeatedly attributes the poem to Shitou, prints the whole verse under the title, quotes individual lines in case commentary, and groups it with named Chan compositions such as the Trust-in-Mind Inscription and Song of Realizing the Way. The primary target translates the title in this attested Chan bibliographic use.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師著參同契一篇。辭旨幽𤀹頗有注解大行於世。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Transmission of the Lamp biography says Shitou wrote one Accord of Difference and Sameness, whose wording was deep and for which explanations circulated widely.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南嶽石頭和尚參同契南嶽石頭和尚參同契竺土大仙心。東西密相付。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Transmission of the Lamp prints the composition under 'The Accord of Difference and Sameness by Master Shitou of Nanyue' and preserves its opening line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有一片言語喚作參同契。末上云。竺土大僊心無過此語也。中間也只隨時說話。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In a Qingliang discourse, the title is explicitly called the name of a piece of wording and its opening is quoted; the occurrence is under another master's discourse, so no Shitou occurrence link.

Occurrences.Kwic: 石頭初看肇論，至會萬物為己者，其惟聖人乎，則曰：聖人無己，靡所不己。乃作參同契
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Joint Essentials of the Lamps retrospectively links Shitou's composition of the verse to his reading of the saying that the sage has no self and nothing is not himself.

Occurrences.Kwic: 承言須會宗，勿自立規矩。觸目不會道，運足焉知路。進步非近遠，迷隔山河固。謹白參玄人，光陰莫虗度。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Lodging Hermitage Draft prints the poem's closing lines: meet the source on hearing words, establish no private rules, and do not waste daylight.

Senses.Explanation: To join, attend, or report to the communal hall. Biographical records use the expression for formal admission: people seeking to join the hall might wait for months, while a favored visitor is admitted that same day; Wuzu orders Yuanwu to join the hall immediately, after which Yuanwu enters the attendants' quarters. In encounter records the imperative 'go to the hall' regularly closes or dismisses an exchange. Wuju says it after striking two visitors, and Wenshu Siye shouts it to a former butcher, who then goes down to the hall. In commentary on the rhinoceros-fan case, a monk tells the entire assembly to go to the hall, and Yuanwu explicitly says that the monk has seized the authority of the host. The institutional and imperative uses share the same hall-directed action.
Senses.Note: The corpus has 529 matches in 137 files. The imperative 'go to the hall' accounts for 349 matches in 99 files, including seven matches in six files that address the whole assembly. The nominal form 'those who seek or attend the hall' occurs four times in four files; 'ordered him immediately to join the hall' occurs ten times in ten files, and 'then went down to the hall' occurs nineteen times in sixteen. These forms distinguish this institutional use of 'join' from other senses of the first graph elsewhere in Chan vocabulary.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。汝既不會。後面箇師僧祇對看。紹擬近前。師便打。曰。信知同坑無異土。參堂去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wuju tells one visitor, 'Since you do not understand, let the monk behind you answer.' When Shao is about to approach, Wuju strikes him and says, 'Indeed, the same pit has no different earth. Go to the hall.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 病痊尋歸。祖一見而喜令即參堂。便入侍者寮方半月。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu's biography says that after recovering and returning, he was welcomed by Wuzu, who ordered him immediately to join the hall; he then entered the attendants' quarters.

Occurrences.Kwic: 時四方來學雲趨水赴，求參堂者或累旬月而不得。間有得者，如登龍門。師徑懷香詣方丈相看。佛鑑顧師敦厖，識為法器。即日歸堂，眾皆驚訝。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A biographical record says that visitors came from all directions, and those seeking admission to the hall sometimes waited for months without obtaining it. This visitor went directly to the abbot's quarters; Fojian received him and returned him to the hall that same day, astonishing the assembly.

Occurrences.Kwic: 時有一禪客出云。大眾參堂去。這僧奪得主家權柄。道得也殺道。只道得八成。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In commentary on the rhinoceros-fan case, a Chan visitor comes forward and says, 'Assembly, go to the hall.' Yuanwu comments, 'This monk seized the authority of the host. Though he said it indeed, he only said eighty percent.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 殊曰：你正殺猪時，見箇甚麼便乃剃頭行脚？師遂作鼓刀勢。殊喝曰：者屠兒參堂去！師便下參堂。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wenshu asks a former butcher, 'When you were killing pigs, what did you see that made you shave your head and travel on foot?' The man makes a knife-wielding gesture. Wenshu shouts, 'You butcher, go to the hall!' The man then goes down to the hall.

Senses.Explanation: (參) = to investigate, consult, look into (as one 參 a teacher or 參究 a matter); (禪) = Chan. (參禪) is the recorded activity of investigating Chan, which the corpus binds to the one great matter of life and death. Gaofeng Yuanmiao states its temper: (參禪須是鐵漢) — to investigate Chan one must be an iron man — (著手心頭便判) (the moment you set to it the mind is decided). He binds it to the one great matter: (只遮生死一大事)，(乃是參禪學道之喉襟) (this single great matter of life-and-death is the very throat-and-collar of investigating Chan and studying the Way), and states the comparison plainly: (資生貴圖求富)，(參禪貴圖求悟) (as making a living prizes seeking wealth, investigating Chan prizes seeking awakening). Zhongfeng Mingben describes people who say they investigate Chan while doing so only with their mouths: (人心浮淺口說參禪) — shallow-minded people 'investigate Chan' only with their mouths, wanting to understand the recorded exchanges as material for conversation, (初無一念要决了生死大事之心) (without a single thought of resolving the great matter). Later records pair the expression with looking at sayings (看話). Render it as ‘investigate Chan,’ following the literal ‘consult / look into’ sense; note the fixed collocation (參禪學道) ('investigate Chan and study the Way'). The records also define the word by its concrete referent: Shitian Faxun (石田法薰) writes (參方衲子)，(出一藂林)，(入一藂林)，(撥草瞻風)，(不憚寒暑)，(喚作參禪) (wandering monks leaving one grove and entering another, parting the grass to gaze at the wind, undeterred by cold and heat — this is 'called 參禪'), then immediately presses (畢竟禪作麼生參) (but after all, how is Chan investigated?) (X70n1386). Shiwu Qinggong opens an evening address: (現前一眾久在叢林)，(謂之參禪)、(謂之辦道)，(殊不知一念未生已前更無別物)，(纔擬心時錯了也) (this assembly has long been in the groves — it is called investigating Chan, called working at the Way — quite unaware that before one thought arises there is no other thing; the instant the mind deliberates, it has already gone wrong) (X70n1399; raised again in 列祖提綱錄 X64n1260). Baichi (百癡) turns the word on itself at a (小參) (informal address): (無禪可參是名參禪)，(無道可悟是名悟道) (no Chan that can be investigated — that is named investigating Chan; no Way that can be awakened to — that is named awakening to the Way) (J28nB202). Two stock formulas recur: (參禪無秘訣)，(只要生死切) (investigating Chan has no secret formula — only that life and death be urgent; 13 hits in 10 allowlist texts, also written 秪要生死切), and the full iron-man quatrain (參禪須是鐵漢)，(著手心頭便判)，(直趣無上菩提)，(一切是非莫管) (25 hits in 20 texts), which the record credits to the layman Li Duwei (李都尉) — (李都尉云)：「(參禪須是鐵漢)，(著手心頭便判)，(直趍無上菩提)，(一切是非莫管)。」 (J26nB183; J26nB182 narrates his awakening verse, 李忽契悟，亦呈偈云).
Senses.Note: Two independently-attributed masters (Gaofeng Yuanmiao 高峰原妙, his 語錄 recorded sayings; Zhongfeng Mingben 中峰明本, his 廣錄 extensive record) use (參禪) (investigate Chan) for the same activity — one framing its temper and aim, one policing genuine vs. mouth-only inquiry. Dahui Zonggao is the acknowledged systematizer of (看話參禪) (‘investigating Chan by looking at sayings’) and is named in the explanation, but no Dahui occurrence is curated here: the strongest Dahui (參禪) passage (T47n1998A, 0864c) sits in a section expounding Linji's (四照用) (his 'four illuminings-and-functions') and invoking Yunmen, where speaker attribution was not cleanly separable, so it was left out per the verify-attribution rule. Zen-scoped grep counts (tag-stripped, 2026-07-11): (參禪) 2950 hits in 336 of the 462 allowlist texts; (參禪學道) 213/111; (參禪人) 135/71; (參禪者) 83/46; (參禪辦道) 4/4. The mouth-only polemic is itself multi-witness: besides Zhongfeng's (口說參禪)。(但欲明悟機緣以資談柄) ('investigate Chan with the mouth only, merely wanting the encounter-stories as talk-fodder'; B25n0145), the (浮石禪師語錄) (Fushi's recorded sayings) has (人心不古)，(口說參禪)，(但欲讀熟幾則機緣以資談柄) ('hearts are not what they were: they investigate Chan with the mouth, only wanting to read up a few encounter-cases as talk-fodder'; J26nB185), and a (五燈全書) (Complete Book of the Five Lamps) verse has (口說參禪心不了) ('the mouth says investigate Chan while the mind is not settled'; X82n1571). The iron-man quatrain Gaofeng deploys is circulating stock credited within the record to the layman Li Duwei (李都尉), not a Gaofeng coinage (J26nB182, J26nB183).

Occurrences.Kwic: 參禪須是鐵漢，著手心頭便判
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (元宵上堂) (Lantern-Festival hall-address, Gaofeng), (高峰原妙禪師語錄) (Gaofeng Yuanmiao's recorded sayings). The temper of investigation: one must be an iron man.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只遮生死一大事，乃是參禪學道之喉襟
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Gaofeng binds (參禪學道) to the one great matter of life and death (its 'throat and collar').

Occurrences.Kwic: 資生貴圖求富，參禪貴圖求悟
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Gaofeng, (上堂): the aim of investigating Chan is (悟) (awakening), as making a living aims at wealth.

Occurrences.Kwic: 人心浮淺口說參禪。但欲明悟機緣以資談柄
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhongfeng Mingben, (天目中峰廣錄): the false (參禪) done only with the mouth, wanting the encounter-stories as talk-fodder.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, to investigate the head of the talk: the word, saying, question, or conversational thread singled out in the record. The compound occurs 187 times in 76 allowlisted texts. The texts specify the raised wording itself: one record identifies an unresolved scripture or public case as the personally investigated word, while Mingben names Zhaozhou's question 'why did Zhaozhou say the word no?' and instructs the listener to investigate that wording and raise great doubt. Other records say to place one's own investigated saying before one, to investigate it earnestly, or criticize merely hunting it in books and other people's mouths. A contrary witness asks what difference there is between those who do and do not perform the associated work. Thus the Zen bend is the selection of actual words from recorded exchanges for sustained investigation; the corpus also records criticism of reifying that activity.
Senses.Note: Translate the term according to its local object—word, saying, question, or conversational thread—and keep every attested imperative as a literal action.

Occurrences.Kwic: 或是經教有所未明、公案有所未透，即此不明不透處便是本參話頭，頓在面前微著眼覷
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The record explicitly identifies the personally investigated wording with what remains unresolved in a scripture or public case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 趙州因甚道箇無字？大要緊只向話頭上堅立志願參，起大疑情參。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Mingben supplies the exact question—why Zhaozhou said the word 'no'—and tells the listener to investigate that wording.

Occurrences.Kwic: 予勸兄弟，各將自己本參話頭著實參去，定有下落。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A direct instruction says to investigate one's own selected saying in earnest.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今參禪人不向自己腳跟下追尋根蒂，返向冊子上他人口角邊覓話頭
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The text criticizes seekers who hunt the wording in books and at other people's mouths.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若謂別有念佛參話頭工夫以為超越者，究竟到頭與未念佛未參話頭者有何差別？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A record explicitly questions the difference between performing and not performing the associated work.

Senses.Explanation: A verb or verbal noun for visiting or attending (參) and making inquiry or requesting instruction (請): "visit and inquire." It occurs 243 times in 121 allowlisted texts. Chinese Chan records show both its institutional and encounter uses. A monk may leave one teacher, travel to another place, and "join the assembly to visit and inquire" (隨眾參請); another biography says that at Shishuang he merely followed the assembly and "no longer visited and inquired" (更不參請). The monastic regulations place "traveling from place to place to visit and inquire" (遊方參請) under a heading that literally lists departure from one's teacher, seeking a respected elder, requesting lodging, first reporting to the guest office, and next registering at the hall office. The term can also describe the encounter itself: a visitor "bent his knees to visit and inquire" (屈膝參請), after which the teacher addressed his understanding; members of an assembly visited and inquired morning and evening while the teacher answered them without weariness (晨夕參請，師與唱酬無倦). The recorded actions are visits, institutional participation, questions, and responses in Chinese Chan texts.
Senses.Note: Productive constructions mark the same range: "join the assembly to visit and inquire" (隨眾參請, 23 occurrences), "enter the room to visit and inquire" (入室參請, 2), "travel from place to place to visit and inquire" (遊方參請, 6), and headings for "circumstances of visiting and inquiry" (參請因緣, 2). Fayan can ask what scripture someone reads "apart from visiting and inquiry" (於參請外), placing it among the ordinary activities of a visitor's life. The Blue Cliff Record contrasts a superintendent's not having "visited and inquired or entered the room" (不曾參請入室) with Fayan subsequently asking why he does not come enter the room. The overlap between travel, residence in an assembly, and direct exchange is native to the term, so these are kept as deployments of one sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師聞此語。禮辭至韶陽。隨眾參請。不言來處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: After hearing the instruction, the monk bows farewell, reaches Shaoyang, and joins the assembly to visit and inquire without saying where he came from.

Occurrences.Kwic: 後到石霜。但隨眾而已。更不參請。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: At Shishuang, the visitor merely follows the assembly and no longer visits and inquires. The negative construction defines the expected institutional action by its absence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 眼問曰。子於參請外。看甚麼經。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Fayan asks what scripture the visitor reads apart from visiting and inquiry, marking the term as an ordinary category of his activity.

Occurrences.Kwic: 遊方參請遊方參請稟辭師長。慕有道尊宿處。依棲求掛搭古規首到客司相看。次往堂司掛搭。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Institutional heading and procedure: leave one's teacher; seek a respected elder; request lodging; first report to the guest office; next register at the hall office.

Occurrences.Kwic: 企靈隱泰道眼精明，乃屈膝參請焉。泰甞謂師曰：我舉拂子，你便向拂子上會；
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A visitor esteems Lingyin Tai's discerning eye, bends his knees to visit and inquire, and is then directly addressed by Tai.

Occurrences.Kwic: 晨夕參請，師與唱酬無倦，一時達者稱為大慧再來。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Morning and evening the assembly visits and inquires, and the teacher responds without weariness.

Occurrences.Kwic: 也不曾參請入室。一日法眼問云。則監院何不來入室。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The superintendent had never visited and inquired or entered the room; Fayan then asks why he does not come enter the room.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'mind' (心) and 'seal' or 'stamp' (印). The term occurs 1,374 times in 280 allowed texts and is repeatedly transmitted, received, secretly entrusted, applied, and tested in lineage records. One assembly address says, 'The ancestral mind-seal is neither long nor short, square nor round, inside nor outside, nor in between' (祖師心印，非長非短，非方非圓，非內非外，亦非中間). Another says it has 'no trace and no shape,' remains distinct through successive ages, and has never been interrupted (祖師心印，無痕無狀。歷劫分明，未嘗間斷). Fengxue's recorded formulation compares it to the mechanism of an iron ox: 'going, it seals and holds; staying, it seals and breaks' (去即印住。住即印破). A lamp address enumerates three applications: 'one seal seals empty space, one seals water, one seals mud' (一印印空。一印印水。一印印泥). An early record extends the stamp grammar in both directions: Bodhidharma 'secretly transmitted the mind-seal, sealing your own mind; mind seals the teaching, the teaching seals mind' (密傳心印印汝本心。以心印法，以法印心). Sengna draws a direct contrast: 'the ancestral mind-seal does not consist exclusively in harsh conduct' (祖師心印非專苦行). These are the corpus's own formal, material, and transmission predicates; the article does not turn the seal into an imported object.
Senses.Note: Required definition formulas found no single prose gloss of the bare compound, but several direct shape-negations and seal-mechanism explanations. 'Ancestral mind-seal' (祖師心印) occurs 336 times in 145 texts, while 'mind-seal of buddhas and ancestors' (佛祖心印) occurs 23 times in 17. Some hits are the bestowed title or name 'Mind-seal' borne by particular monks; those proper-name uses were excluded from the technical sense evidence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖師心印，非長非短，非方非圓，非內非外，亦非中間。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Complete Collection, Chuming Baoyin section. The master gives a sequence of direct shape and location negations for the ancestral mind-seal; no roster link was asserted.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖師心印，無痕無狀。歷劫分明，未嘗間斷。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continuation of the Lamp from the Jianzhong-Jingguo Era. An assembly address denies trace and shape while stating continuity through successive ages.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖師心印。狀似鐵牛之機。去即印住。住即印破。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Compendium raises Fengxue's iron-ox mechanism formulation. As a transmitted case with a later section setting, it remains unkeyed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖師心印。一印印空。一印印水。一印印泥。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Transmission of the Lamp. The assembly address explicitly applies seals to empty space, water, and mud. The nearest lineage heading does not yield a safe roster link.

Occurrences.Kwic: 密傳心印印你本心以心印法以法印心心既如此法亦如此
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Ancient Worthies describes Bodhidharma's transmission to Huike and expands the seal grammar between mind and teaching. It is retrospective narration, so MasterName is null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖師心印非專苦行。但助道耳。若契本心發隨意真光之用。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of the Transmission of the Lamp, Sengna section. Sengna tells Huiman that the ancestral mind-seal is not exclusively harsh conduct and contrasts two uses of such conduct.

Senses.Explanation: Literally "mind" (心) and "ground" (地): "mind-ground," attested 1,568 times in 268 allowlisted texts. Huangbo's record calls it the "mind-ground gate" and says, "all things are established depending on this mind; meeting a scene, they exist; without a scene, they do not" (萬法皆依此心建立，遇境即有，無境即無). A transmission verse says, "mind-ground is originally unborn; the causal ground arises following conditions; conditions and seeds do not obstruct one another; flower and fruit are likewise" (心地本無生，因地從緣起，緣種不相妨，華果亦復爾). Another verse says it "contains all seeds" and that universal rain makes them sprout (心地含諸種，普雨悉皆萌). In a repeatedly raised exchange, Yunfeng answers "What is the mind-ground gate?" with "it is not obtained from another" (不從人得). The word also forms "mind-ground seal" (心地印, 132 occurrences) and "mind-ground gate" (心地法門, 157).
Senses.Note: The ground image is productive: seeds are contained, rain makes them sprout, and flower and fruit follow. Later records preserve conflicting enacted labels: one teacher raises a staff and says, "this is the mind-ground seal" (這箇是心地印), while another raises a staff and says it is not the seal. These are recorded deployments, not separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 所謂心地法門。萬法皆依此心建立。遇境即有無境即無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Huangbo's record defines the mind-ground gate through things being established depending on this mind. The section is clear, but the occurrence remains unlinked for conservative attribution.

Occurrences.Kwic: 心地本無生因地從緣起緣種不相妨華果亦復爾
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A transmission verse: mind-ground is originally unborn; the causal ground arises following conditions; conditions and seeds do not obstruct one another; flower and fruit are likewise.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雲峰因僧問：如何是心地法門？峰曰：不從人得。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A raised Yunfeng exchange: asked what the mind-ground gate is, Yunfeng says it is not obtained from another.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拈起拄杖，云：「這箇是心地印。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In instruction, the teacher raises a staff and says, "this is the mind-ground seal."

Occurrences.Kwic: 所以六祖云。心地含諸種。普雨悉皆萌。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Hongzhi quotes the Sixth Patriarch: mind-ground contains all seeds; universal rain makes them sprout.

AlternateTargets: outside mind there is no separate thing
Senses.Explanation: Literally, "outside mind, no thing stands." The phrase occurs 199 times in 100 allowlisted texts. Here the graph translated as "thing" or "what is established" (法) is contextual: in the recurring pair "this thing is mind; outside mind no thing stands; this mind is the thing; outside it no mind stands" (此法即心，心外無法；此心即法，法外無心), it names what could be set up as a thing apart, not an untranslated religious loanword. Shao's frequently quoted verse places the phrase beside visible landscape: "the summit of Tongxuan is not the human world; outside mind no thing stands; blue mountains fill the eyes" (通玄峰頂，不是人間；心外無法，滿目青山). A later master quotes that verse and says it has been "broken into two pieces" (打成兩橛). Another hall address strikes the Chan seat and asks: "mind has not arisen—where could the things be established? Where did mountains, rivers, and the great earth come from?" (心既不生，法從何立？山河大地，甚處得來). The corpus therefore records the line as a maxim, a verse, a question to the assembly, and an object of later criticism; this entry does not decide the criticism.
Senses.Note: The graph translated as "thing" or "what is established" (法) is resolved from the syntax of each quoted line. Its singular form is rendered "thing" or "what is established," while the plural compound "the myriad things" (萬法) is rendered according to its local syntax. The evidence does not warrant a separate sense merely because later speakers approve, question, quote, or criticize the same proposition.

Occurrences.Kwic: 此法即心，心外無法。此心即法，法外無心。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The paired formulation makes mind and the named thing reciprocal and denies either outside the other.

Occurrences.Kwic: 通玄峰頂，不是人間。心外無法，滿目青山。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Shao's verse: “the summit of Tongxuan is not the human world; outside mind no thing stands; blue mountains fill the eyes.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂，拍禪床曰：心外無法，萬法唯心。心既不生，法從何立？山河大地，甚處得來？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A hall address strikes the Chan seat, states the formula, and follows it with questions about establishment and the mountains, rivers, and earth.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂，舉韶國師曰：通玄峰頂，不是人間。心外無法，滿目青山。師召大眾曰：韶國師好個頌子，只是打成兩橛。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later hall address quotes Shao's verse, calls it a fine verse, and says it is split into two pieces.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'mind-precept.' The phrase occurs 45 times in 27 allowlisted texts. Some hits are names, but direct Chan sermons make a technical deployment explicit. One says, 'mind is precept, precept is mind; mind and precept are not two.' Another contrasts mind-precept with form-precept, calls precept itself mind, and describes the form-precept through robes, bowl, and staff. A further sermon says its mind-precept is originally pure and has no contamination, explicitly contrasting a thought that seeks to receive some separate precept outside mind. Earlier lamp narratives say that laymen personally received a master's mind-precept; one adds that Bai Juyi repeatedly sat facing the master with no speech. The compound therefore also names something transmitted in a teacher-student relation. The Zen bend is attested in these equations, contrasts, and transmission notices: mind is made the locus and substance of precept, without making the precept optional.
Senses.Note: Name-like uses were excluded from the definition. The re-grounding is stated only from passages that directly equate or contrast mind and precept.

Occurrences.Kwic: 既於山僧處求受心地戒法，須知即心是戒、即戒是心，心戒無二，萬善從生。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A sermon gives the direct equation: mind is precept, precept is mind, and the two are not separate.

Occurrences.Kwic: 戒有兩般，心無二用。兩般者，心戒、相戒；二用者，體持、用持。戒者，心也；衣者，意也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A sermon explicitly contrasts mind-precept and form-precept and says precept is mind.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉一念于心外求受別戒，早自埋沒己靈。蓋此心戒者，的體淨潔，了無纖染
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The speaker rejects seeking a separate precept outside mind and describes this mind-precept as wholly clean and without contamination.

Occurrences.Kwic: 公親受南泉心戒。大夫問南泉：「弟子家中有一片石。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A lamp narrative says Lu Gen personally received Nanquan's mind-precept before recording their stone-Buddha exchange.

Occurrences.Kwic: 白舍人親受心戒，又時對坐，並無言說。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A separate lamp narrative says Bai Juyi personally received the mind-precept and repeatedly sat facing the master without speech.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the place of mental activity is extinguished
AlternateTargets: the locus of mind's activity is gone
Senses.Explanation: Literally, the "place" (處) of the mind's "activity" or "movement" (心行) is "extinguished" (滅): "the place of mental activity is extinguished," attested 128 times in 65 allowlisted texts. The standard companion is "the road of language is cut off" (言語道斷, 171 occurrences). A transmission record explains the parallel syntax: "when principle is clear, the road of language is cut off—what words could discuss it? When the purport is met, the place of mental activity is extinguished—what contemplation could think it?" (理明則言語道斷，何言之能議；旨會則心行處滅，何觀之能思). Hongzhi asks, "just when the road of language is cut off and the place of mental activity is extinguished, what then?" (言語道斷心行處滅，又作麼生). A later address quotes "it cannot be known by wisdom or recognized by consciousness; the road of language is cut off, the place of mental activity extinguished," then answers with a deliberate counter-formulation: "it can also be known by wisdom and recognized by consciousness; the road of language is cut off, mental activity is not extinguished" (心行不滅). Zhongfeng also reports an interpreter's equation: "cut off thought, then the place of mental activity is extinguished" (絕慮則心行處滅), before contesting that line of equation in the following passage. The entry therefore records the fixed pair, explicit parallel, question, and counter-witness rather than equating the phrase with blankness.
Senses.Note: The exact counter-form "mental activity is not extinguished" (心行不滅) occurs twice. "When the purport is met, the place of mental activity is extinguished" (旨會則心行處滅) occurs six times; Zhongfeng's "cut off thought" equation occurs once. The phrase is paired with language but also appears independently in later addresses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 理明則言語道斷。何言之能議。旨會則心行處滅。何觀之能思。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Transmission-lamp prose gives the explicit parallel: "when principle is clear, the road of language is cut off; when the purport is met, the place of mental activity is extinguished." The historical section remains unlinked.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不可以智知，不可以識識，言語道斷，心行處滅。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A formal address quotes: "it cannot be known by wisdom or recognized by consciousness; the road of language is cut off and the place of mental activity extinguished."

Occurrences.Kwic: 不可以智知，不可以識識，言語道斷，心行處滅。保寧道：亦可以智知，亦可以識識，言語道斷，心行不滅。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The same address joins the quoted line to Baoning's counter: "it can also be known by wisdom and recognized by consciousness; the road of language is cut off and mental activity is not extinguished." The longer exact span retains the headword as well as the unique counter-witness.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祇如言語道斷心行處滅。又作麼生。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Hongzhi asks: "just when the road of language is cut off and the place of mental activity is extinguished, what then?"

Occurrences.Kwic: 絕言則言語道斷。絕慮則心行處滅。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhongfeng reports an interpreter's pairing: "cut off words, then the road of language is cut off; cut off thought, then the place of mental activity is extinguished." The following prose contests this equation, so it is not assigned as Zhongfeng's definition.
